Thanks Daniel — pulling this together now. High level: Redwood supports region affinity with an operational pin (customer-configured) plus a short failover window for transient telemetry; we can provide acceptance criteria that distinguish between request-path routing (pinned) and asynchronous analytics (configurable opt-out).

I’ve attached a concise acceptance checklist (redwood-geo-acceptance-checklist.pdf) and a current subprocessor roster extract (subprocessor-roster-2026-09.csv) meant for contract review. Quick notes in the checklist:

- Binding scope: customer data processed by the inference runtime and KV cache will be pinned to the EU region unless explicit temporary failover is triggered by capacity or an ops incident.
- Telemetry: control-plane metrics + anonymized usage telemetry are collected; we provide a toggle to limit telemetry export to regional telemetry collectors.
- Failover window: transient cross-region hop is limited to 72 hours for emergency restorations and must be logged to the customer audit stream.
- Operational evidence: we include recent runbook excerpts and an ops contact for on-call validation.

Please treat the CSV as an internal disclosure for review — it contains the subprocessor names, roles, and last-validated date. If you want an expanded compliance pack (SOCs, attestations), say the word and I’ll route to our Security team.

Chloe Martin
Head of Customer Security (EMEA)
Redwood Inference
